design.renew: commit() renews through the job authority's existing heartbeatUspJobAttempt after every named package, committed, skipped or refused; jobs.ts is unchanged.
design.leaseLost: A 409 from the attempt assertion in pinned() or from the renewal becomes AppError 503 INTAKE_RUN_LEASE_LOST, which intakeRunRefusal already reads as infrastructure; fail() returns without writing, so no target is stopped and no refusal sentence or retry mark is written. The authority's next claim follows the lease expiry.
design.retry: commitOne already skips a package that is COMMITTED at its named revision + 1; the retry re-records its targets idempotently and commits only the rest.
design.refusal: A package refused by its own checks keeps today's path: its targets stop in its own words, other packages continue, and the job fails with its code.
design.seam: getPackage joins intakeRunSteps as 'package' so a check can supply package state; every call site in the worker uses it.

added: a confirmation run renews its lease after each committed package (3 packages, 3 renewals)
a lease lost after package 2 stops nothing, and the retry commits only package 3 (no stop, no job error, attempt 2 commits [3], 5 renewals in total)

gaps: No runtime walk: a 21-package confirmation on a live box (G05) is still needed to show the lease is held in practice.
A single commitPackage call longer than the 180 s lease cannot renew inside it (that would need areas.ts; commit cost per feature is D4). The lease-lost path then still ends the attempt cleanly.
The target and prepare phases do not renew: each is one target or one review, bounded and observed well under half the lease (LQ1b: 12 s to the first card).
A lease lost between the last renewal and acceptUspJobAttempt is still reported through acceptance's own conflict; fail() then cannot write and the job is retried, as before.
